  Dynamic driving scene reconstruction has made remarkable strides in recent years by leveraging generative priors, particularly in the quality of novel trajectory rendering. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains between the generated data and real-world sensor observations, severely hindering further improvements in reconstruction fidelity. In this paper, we present ReconDreamer#, a self-evolving framework that synergizes reconstruction and generation for dynamic driving scenes, which substantially bridges the gap between synthesized novel trajectory data and recorded real-world observations. Within this self-evolving closed-loop framework, the generative and reconstruction models mutually reinforce each other through iterative refinement, ultimately yielding a significant enhancement in the 3D representation capability of the reconstruction model. Additionally, we introduce a geometry-prior-based adaptive ground model to further enhance the rendering quality of the reconstruction model. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct comprehensive evaluations on Waymo, nuScenes, PandaSet, and EUVS benchmarks. Specifically on Waymo, at a 6-m lateral shift, ReconDreamer# improves NTA-IoU and NTL-IoU by 8.8% and 3.0%, respectively, and reduces FID by 15.1% relative to ReconDreamer++.
  </details>

- **[What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04164)**  `arXiv:2611.04164`  
  _Lixuan He, Jihyeon Je, Yang You, Leonidas Guibas_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Long-horizon video generation is increasingly moving toward autoregressive rollout, where each newly generated segment becomes part of the evidence used for future prediction. Recent causal decoders, long-context training, and KV-cache mechanisms have extended feasible duration, but most inference pipelines still decide the visible past implicitly through recent windows, compressed caches, or external memory. This raises a direct question: \textbf{can the choice of which past frames or segments to show to the decoder be treated as an explicit test-time decision?} We answer this question with \textsc{ReCR}, a training-free method that formulates autoregressive video decoding as representation-guided context rewriting. At each step, \textsc{ReCR} builds a selected visible context from the generated history by using internal decoder representations to favor context units that match the global rollout state, avoid redundancy with the recent continuation, preserve temporal boundary coverage, and widen the range of spatial layouts in view. The selected units are then mapped onto a compact causal axis before decoding the next block. Across long-horizon text-to-video benchmarks, \textsc{ReCR} consistently improves multiple autoregressive backbones under matched visible-token budgets. Empirical analyses such as representation-space diagnostics and transition-count prompt switching further show that improving what remains visible is an effective path toward more stable long-video decoding.
  </details>

- **[Improving PI-RADS Prediction and Prostate Cancer Detection from Multiparametric MRI with Anatomical Guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04155)**  `arXiv:2611.04155`  
  _Seungbin Park, Thibault Heintz, Rachit Saluja, Francesca Khani, Timothy McClure, Daniel Margolis, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Accurate prediction of Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) scores from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) remains challenging, more so than clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) detection. Given the importance of lesion location in PI-RADS scoring, we evaluated whether incorporating prostate zonal masks improves PI-RADS prediction and csPCa detection across multiple architectures (3D ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ViT) using a large-scale internal dataset. Anatomical guidance generally improved performance across architectures, with the best results achieved by ResNet-18 with 2-zone guidance for PI-RADS prediction (QWK = 0.511) and ResNet-50 with 5-zone guidance for csPCa detection (AUC = 0.809). Fine-tuned results on external datasets further demonstrated the benefits of anatomical guidance. Furthermore, models with anatomical guidance improved the utility of model-predicted PI-RADS scores for PI-RADS-based csPCa detection (positive defined as PI-RADS>=3). Combining model-predicted and expert-assigned PI-RADS scores significantly increased the AUC from 0.711 to 0.756 (p < 0.05), suggesting that AI-derived PI-RADS scores may provide complementary information to expert assessment for csPCa detection. Overall, our findings highlight the value of incorporating prostate zonal anatomy into deep learning-based prostate MRI assessment.
  </details>

- **[Co-Occurrence Priors Override Visual Spatial Evidence: Understanding False Alarms in Vision-Language Models for Construction Struck-By Hazard Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04112)**  `arXiv:2611.04112`  
  _Xiaoshan Zhou_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly support construction hazard monitoring, yet their frequent false alarms remain poorly understood. This study investigates whether false struck-by hazard warnings arise from failures in object recognition, spatial relation encoding, or hazard decisions dominated by learned co-occurrence priors. We evaluated Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B using 355 counterfactual worker-excavator scene pairs with controlled spatial proximity and worker-removal variants, combining behavioral analysis, internal representation probing, causal interventions, and decision correction. Both models recognized the entities and encoded their spatial relations (out-of-fold AUROC: 0.82 and 0.91), assigning higher hazard scores to near than far scenes in 79% and 73% of pairs. Nevertheless, 74% and 100% of far scenes were falsely classified as hazardous. Removing the worker reduced Qwen's hazard rate to 11%, while worker presence exerted 2.4- and 3.2-times greater influence on hazard scores than spatial proximity in the respective models. Attention-head interventions, neuron-level interventions, and activation steering failed to eliminate this co-occurrence bias. However, conditioning hazard decisions on the model's own spatial-relation representation improved Qwen's specificity from 0.36 to 0.58 at matched sensitivity, outperforming threshold recalibration. These findings reveal that VLM struck-by false alarms stem primarily from decision-making failures rather than deficiencies in object recognition or spatial encoding, suggesting that future efforts should prioritize conditioning hazard decisions on encoded spatial evidence rather than further improving visual recognition alone.
  </details>

- **[Is This 3D Asset Usable? Beyond the Beauty Render for Asset Curation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04102)**  `arXiv:2611.04102`  
  _Rushikesh Zawar, Vladimir Kim_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Large 3D repositories make it easy to collect assets, but difficult to determine whether they can be reused reliably across scene assembly, editing, rendering, game production, and training-data construction. An asset can look plausible in RGB while hiding disconnected geometry, problematic UV organization, or materials that fail to resolve correctly after import. We introduce Diagnostic Rendered Evidence (DRE): aligned beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe views scored by pass-specific frozen ViT classifiers and combined through late fusion. On 1,234 human labeled TexVerse assets, nested grouped evaluation achieves 86.36% balanced accuracy and 88.32% bad-asset recall. On a separate, balanced 764 external reference test, DRE achieved 88.9% balanced reference-label accuracy. Our method requires only an imported asset and renderer-derived evidence, without repository identity, creator, popularity, text, or source metadata at inference. Our results support cross-corpus portability and show that purpose built diagnostic views expose defects that just the beauty views can miss. Webpage:this https URL
  </details>

- **[CHROMA-MILL: Joint Low-Light Enhancement and White Balance under Colored Illumination](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04092)**  `arXiv:2611.04092`  
  _Pol Riubrogent-Comas, David Serrano-Lozano, Maria Pilligua, Michael S. Brown, Ramon Baldrich, Javier Vazquez-Corral_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Capturing an image in a low-light environment produces a weak, noisy sensor signal. Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to restore it. Auto white balance (AWB) is also required for every image, and the same noisy signal degrades its ability to infer the scene illuminant. LLIE is typically performed first, followed by AWB, but this strategy remains largely unexamined because existing low-light datasets span a narrow range of illuminants and lack illuminant ground truth for evaluating AWB. We address this with CHROMA-MILL, a RAW dataset of 50 scenes captured with a DSLR and smartphone under four calibrated illuminants at eleven intensity levels. Because light is additive, we blend these captures in the linear RAW domain to synthesize physically valid illuminant mixtures with exact chromaticity ground truth. Benchmarking on this data, we find joint correction is best, and introduce CTI-Retinexformer, which supervises an illumination map, a chromaticity prediction, and an illumination-invariant scene embedding, outperforming the best cascade by 0.7 dB PSNR$_L$ and 1.1 $\Delta E_{00}$.
  </details>

- **[ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04087)**  `arXiv:2611.04087`  
  _Tianyi Ma, Jing Gu, Haozhe Zhao, Liang Chen, Yunfan Zhang, Haijun Su, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Scientific discovery builds on accurate observations interpreted through domain knowledge and reasoning. For scientific 3D data, this requires understanding structures and spatial relationships, from protein contacts to anatomical organization. Existing multimodal benchmarks largely evaluate text and 2D images, while scientific 3D evaluations vary in representations and protocols across disciplines, limiting cross-disciplinary comparison. To assess these foundational capabilities, we introduce ScienceVision, a cross-domain benchmark for scientific 3D understanding and reasoning through expert-level visual question answering (VQA). We construct 250 questions, with 50 each from Biology, Chemistry, Medical Imaging, Mechanical CAD, and Architecture, through a pipeline combining synthetic question generation with domain-expert review and annotation. Each task pairs a native 3D artifact with a scientific question, a specified response format, and a task-specific reference answer, requiring domain knowledge to be applied to geometric or topological evidence. We evaluate 12 models on the same questions in three settings: visual question answering with native 3D artifacts accessed through an agent harness's file and code-execution tools; the same workflow augmented with expert-inspired viewer inspection and measurement tools exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP); and visual question answering from prescribed rendered 2D images using an agent harness. All settings use the same task-specific deterministic final-answer scoring. The inspection environment supports view changes, target isolation, and slice inspection. In this main comparison, the best mean answer score is 0.53 out of 1. Mean scores in the native-artifact workflow without additional MCP tools exceed those in the rendered-image workflow for every model, by 17.2 percentage points on average.
  </details>

- **[From Visual Matching to Textual Conditioning: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation via Reference Inversion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04084)**  `arXiv:2611.04084`  
  _Jiahao Nie, Yun Xing, Wenbin An, Qixin Zhang, Yap-Peng Tan, Alex C. Kot, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment objects from unseen domains using only a few annotated references. Recent Segment Anything Model (SAM)-based methods have advanced CD-FSS, yet their reference-target visual matching is highly sensitive to target appearance variations. SAM3 introduces text-conditioned segmentation, enabling natural-language descriptions to guide segmentation across target images, but directly using the category name as the condition still yields unstable performance under severe domain shifts. We propose Reference Inversion for SAM3 (RI-SAM3) that leverages SAM3's large-scale vision-language pre-training to learn suitable textual tokens for each target category. RI-SAM3 comprises three core designs: (i) Bi-level Reference Inversion that learns complementary tokens before and after the frozen text encoder: the former remain anchored in SAM3's text space while the latter represent the category more flexibly; (ii) Layer-adaptive Textual Conditioning combines these tokens differently as object queries evolve across decoder layers; and (iii) Presence-aware Confidence Supervision that jointly supervises query confidence and target presence for reliable predictions. With SAM3 frozen, RI-SAM3 optimizes around 12K parameters only per category and it efficiently segments each target in a single forward pass with reusable textual conditioning without per-sample reference-target visual matching. Extensive experiments over multiple widely adopted benchmarks show that RI-SAM3 achieves superior performance consistently in CD-FSS tasks, together with strong robustness, efficiency, and generalization.
  </details>

- **[Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution and Denoising of Intracardiac 4D Flow MRI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04053)**  `arXiv:2611.04053`  
  _Yusuf A. Ozturk, Jie Zheng, Fanwei Kong_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Intracardiac flow is driven by complex, and time-varying cardiac motion and interaction with the heart valves, producing complex flow features that may provide valuable information for disease diagnosis and treatment planning. 4D Flow MRI enables non-invasive, time-resolved measurement of three-dimensional cardiovascular velocity fields. However, substantial noise and limited spatial and temporal resolution limit its ability to accurately resolve flow features. We propose 4D-MRAR (4D Magnetic Resonance Augmented Reconstruction), a deep learning (DL) method to super-resolve and denoise 4D Flow MRI data. Unlike prior DL methods that train and infer on static vascular regions, our method predicts intracardiac flow within hearts undergoing large deformation. Moreover, it uniquely allows for simultaneous super-resolution in 3D space and time. The method combines a residual convolutional neural network, a recurrent neural network, and an implicit neural field to predict high-resolution velocity and pressure fields while efficiently enforcing the governing equations of fluid flow during training. Trained on a synthetic dataset obtained from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of left ventricle (LV) flow, our method generalizes to synthetic whole-heart 4D flow MRI data, and demonstrated promising performance on real 4D Flow MRI. The produced super-resolved flow fields exhibit significantly improved accuracy and greater consistency with the governing equations of blood flow compared with prior methods.
  </details>

- **[Do Pretrained Backbones Transfer to Physical Sensors? A Systematic Study of Multimodal Initialization Across the Sensor Stack](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04034)**  `arXiv:2611.04034`  
  _Fabio Montello, Ronja Güldenring, Lucas Mogensen Sandby, Christoffer Koo Øhrstrøm, Lazaros Nalpantidis_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Transfer learning from pretrained backbones has become standard practice in multi-sensor computer vision---yet two questions remain open: which pretrained weights transfer best to multi-sensor setups, and can in-domain pretraining outperform off-the-shelf solutions? Frameworks like MultiMAE demonstrate the utility of masked autoencoding in a multi-modal context, but rely entirely on dense, model-derived modalities. It is unclear how robustly these methods translate to real-world applications that use physical sensors, where the aggregation of diverse public datasets for large-scale pretraining inherently introduces modality sparsity. To investigate this systematically, we curate a multi-sensor autonomous driving collection of $2.82M$ images from 16 publicly available datasets, incorporating both physical hardware modalities (RGB, LWIR, NIR, Event) and model-derived modalities (Stereo Depth, Segmentation). We use this collection for in-domain pretraining based on the MultiMAE approach. We adapt MultiMAE's loss formulation to accommodate sparse samples, and study the effect of an enforced encoder bottleneck for modality alignment and of additional losses specific to dense reconstruction (SSIM and FFT). We then systematically compare against common pretrained backbones (ViT, MAE, DINO and MultiMAE) across downstream sensor fusion tasks. We find that MultiMAE is a surprisingly strong out-of-the-box baseline, transferring effectively even to modalities it has never seen, while our targeted modifications yield incremental but consistent improvements on multi-sensor transfer and overall robustness.
  </details>

- **[Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization Enables Flexible World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04028)**  `arXiv:2611.04028`  
  _Siqiao Huang, Partha Kaushik, Michael Chen, Hengkai Pan, Kaiwen Geng, Omar Chehab, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Effective world modeling requires compressing salient history information that facilitates future prediction. However, most existing approaches inherit tokenization and conditioning mechanisms from video generation, where objectives are centered around perceptual realism rather than predictive utility. This discrepancy limits the world model's effectiveness, especially in environments dominated by visual nuisances or task-irrelevant background details. To this end, we introduce Compression Forcing (CF), a general framework that aligns history compression with the predictive objective of world modeling. Compression Forcing features Dynamics-Aware Tokenization (DAT), a novel tokenization method that compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. Built on a diffusion backbone, this structure enables Hierarchical History Guidance (HG-H), allowing selective amplification of dynamics-salient information during inference. Extensive experiments across various environments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making performance, establishing Compression Forcing as a highly flexible and effective approach for world modeling.
  </details>

- **[SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04012)**  `arXiv:2611.04012`  
  _Qing Xu, Xiechen Shen, Xianjian He, Guqiao Liang, Zixiao Chai, Jiale Qin, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Surgical scene understanding is pivotal for computer-assisted intervention, yet demands compositional reasoning across instruments, anatomy, and workflow. Existing surgical vision-language models rely on instruction tuning with large-scale question-answer pairs, entailing laborious data curation and costly retraining. To bridge this gap, we propose SurgEye, a perception-reasoning framework that grounds reasoning in a vision foundation model without instruction tuning. Specifically, we devise Routed Multi-Task Perception (RMP) that routes the vision foundation model through task-specific pathways learned from public perception labels, producing spatial and temporal evidence. We further introduce Agentic Compositional Reasoning (ACR) that employs a frozen large language model to coordinate RMP specialists and temporal memory as callable tools, composing evidence across tasks and time into grounded answers. Moreover, we construct SurgEye-Bench spanning eight surgical procedures, pairing each question with perception labels for verifiable evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-arts in surgical reasoning. The source code will be available.
  </details>

- **[Do We Still Need Rotation-Invariant Architectures? A Statistical Robustness Benchmark for Point Cloud Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03952)**  `arXiv:2611.03952`  
  _Abdulla Nasir Chowdhury, Gulpi Qorik Oktagalu Pratamasunu, Kazuhiro Fukui_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  A substantial line of work builds rotation invariance directly into point cloud architectures. We benchmark 10 architectures (PointNet, PointNet++, DGCNN, RIConv, RIConv++, RISurConv, PointMLP, PointTransformer, and the equivariant VN-PointNet and VN-DGCNN) across 5 domains under pose, noise, and occlusion, and analyze the results with confirmatory hypothesis tests rather than point estimates. The three rotation-invariant (RI) architectures achieve the best pose robustness but rank among the lowest on noise robustness in 4 of 5 domains. We ask whether this cost is intrinsic to invariance or specific to how invariance is obtained. We retrain all 10 architectures unchanged, with a simple invariance loss on the embedding and three training seeds each, and evaluate all models on the independently designed ModelNet40-C. Invariance training transfers narrowly but reliably. It improves exactly the corruption families its perturbations target wherever the baseline has headroom (mean occlusion +10.5, lidar +13.4 percentage points of accuracy). At matched training budget the best standard backbone and the best RI architecture end on par on unseen corruptions (within 2.5 percentage points in every seed), and invariance-trained RIConv++ is the most seed-stable top model. Once rotation augmentation is widened, standard backbones concede only a flat, angle-independent accuracy offset under full-sphere rotation. We release the benchmark along with a package for analyzing point cloud robustness and reproducing our results.
  </details>

- **[Camera Radar LiDAR Fusion via Point-Cloud Projection for Multi-Task Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03942)**  `arXiv:2611.03942`  
  _Kavin Chandrasekaran, Sorin Grigorescu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Autonomous vehicles require robust perception systems to operate safely under diverse environmental conditions. While cameras provide high-resolution visual data, their performance significantly degrades in low-light and adverse weather. High Definition (HD) radar offers superior reliability and angular resolution under such conditions but lacks rich visual feature recognition. LiDAR, though expensive, delivers highly precise distance measurements and dense point clouds. Each sensor exhibits unique trade-offs, necessitating the development of advanced sensor fusion algorithms to harness complementary strengths while minimizing computational complexity and maintaining accuracy. In this study, the proposed fusion architecture performs early fusion by combining camera images with perspective-view point cloud data from HD radar and LiDAR sensors. The proposed model is trained to detect vehicles and segment free drivable space simultaneously. Experiments are performed on the RADIal dataset where we demonstrate that fusing point cloud data with camera images in front-view surpasses the performances of the most recent standalone and fusion models.
  </details>

- **[FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03937)**  `arXiv:2611.03937`  
  _Yifan Liu, Baihan Zhang, Khai Loong Aw, Klemen Kotar, Daniel L.K. Yamins_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Humans imagine scene changes under hypothetical motions, an ability central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning. However, this capability remains underexplored in vision-language models and world models. We formalize this capability as Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and introduce FlowBench, a resource for training and evaluating both, with 428K training examples spanning simulated and real-world scenes, household environments and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types. A scalable, fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow. For VLMs, proprietary models exhibit an imagination gap, performing worse when motion outcomes must be inferred than when observed, and open-source models perform near chance; fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on FlowBench-Sim-Train raises its accuracy by 29.5 percentage points in simulation and 16.9 on real images, a strong sim-to-real transfer. For world models, training on FlowBench-Sim improves text-to-flow prediction for all four model families we test, raising the accuracy of Psi-0.6 from 52.1% to 61.7%. FlowBench thus serves as a training and evaluation resource for both. Code and datasets are released atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Beyond Proposals: Region-Consistent Open-Set Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03741)**  `arXiv:2611.03741`  
  _Jiehui Tang, Yunlong Yu, Zhao Wang, Jungong Han_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Open-set object detection (OSOD) suffers from a fundamental limitation under dense proposal mechanisms: highly overlapping proposals associated with the same object are often assigned contradictory known/unknown predictions. Existing methods perform open-set reasoning independently for each proposal, while ignoring the shared semantics among correlated proposals, resulting in fragmented detections and unstable open-set decisions. In this paper, we reformulate OSOD as an object-centric semantic inference problem, where correlated proposals jointly support a coherent region-level semantic decision. Based on this perspective, we propose OCSI-Net, a unified framework that combines object-centric semantic consistency with geometry-aware uncertainty stabilization. Specifically, OCSI-Net aggregates correlated proposals into structured region clusters and infers region-level semantics from aggregated semantic evidence, thereby enforcing coherent open-set predictions within the same object region. Furthermore, a geometry-aware uncertainty mechanism is introduced to stabilize optimization near open-set transition boundaries. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that OCSI-Net consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving the harmonic mean of known and unknown detection by an average of 6.83\% over the second-best method.
  </details>

- **[Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03717)**  `arXiv:2611.03717`  
  _Zhengyang Liu, Jianguo Huang, Junxi Hu, Yucheng Mi, Haojie Cai, Wenxuan Shen, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. To this end, we propose PhysFTM---a physics-informed functional Tucker model that parameterizes the Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) and incorporates PDE constraints through finite-difference residuals evaluated at off-sensor collocation points. These residuals provide additional physical information in regions without direct observational supervision. PhysFTM first reconstructs continuous spatial fields at support frames via an alternating minimization scheme, optimizing the Tucker core tensor and the RKHS-based factors separately. To enable missing-frame reconstruction, PhysFTM constructs a continuous trajectory in Tucker-core space, which is decoded by the learned spatial RKHS-FTM representation to recover the full spatiotemporal field. Experiments on Allen--Cahn, Navier--Stokes, three-dimensional Heat equations, and a three-dimensional gridded Copernicus ocean reanalysis demonstrate accurate 2D/3D reconstruction under two missing-frame protocols. Code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03533)**  `arXiv:2611.03533`  
  _Xudong Cai, Yongcai Wang, Deying Li, Chuanxia Zheng_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  We introduce CoLa3D, a simple and effective model for composable 3D scene decomposition that, given a single whole-scene latent from either a single image or an existing scene mesh as input, directly outputs a set of object meshes with consistent spatial layout that can be assembled back into a coherent scene. CoLa3D introduces a novel paradigm for 3D scene decomposition within a shared whole-scene latent, unlike alternatives that perform per-object generation in canonical spaces and then glue the objects back together with fragile pose and scale estimation. The network is a lightweight, flexible, and scalable query-based transformer that accepts various types of queries, including 2D masks, 3D points, and learnable queries, and learns to decompose the scene into objects in a compact latent space. On both synthetic and real-world datasets, CoLa3D achieves state-of-the-art performance on composable 3D scene decomposition, substantially improving global scene-level consistency and object-level quality while running 2 times faster and using less than 1% of SAM 3D's training data. Visible depth on par with MoGe2 further confirms that latent decomposition preserves accurate visible scene geometry while producing physically complete, decomposable object meshes.
  </details>

- **[TaoMate-FVSR: Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03393)**  `arXiv:2611.03393`  
  _Xinyang Li, Zeran Xu, Jingna Sun, Qijun Gan, Chenwei Zhang, Meiguang Jin, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Low-quality facial videos suffer from missing fine details, while AI-generated videos may additionally contain implausible teeth and lip movements that do not match the speech. Restoring the mouth region is particularly challenging: enhancing existing details can preserve structural errors, whereas regenerating them risks changing facial identity and articulation. We propose an audio-guided facial video restoration framework that reconstructs unreliable mouth details and aligns lip movements with the speech while preserving facial identity and temporal consistency. Built on a video diffusion transformer, our framework mixes input video latents with noise to retain useful source information while allowing corrupted details to be regenerated. Audio guides lip movements, reference images constrain facial appearance, and previously generated frames promote temporal consistency. We train the model in two stages, first learning visual restoration from degraded images and videos, then learning audio-guided lip correction from degraded dubbed videos. The resulting model supports both restoration with the original audio and visual dubbing with replacement audio. On talking-head restoration benchmarks, our method achieves the lowest LPIPS and DISTS and the best lip synchronization scores among the evaluated restoration baselines. Qualitative results on AI-generated videos further show improvements in facial detail and mouth-region appearance, including clearer tooth boundaries and lip contours.
  </details>

- **[TME-ContextNet: Class-Conditioned Spatial Supervision and Grouped Decoding for Joint Nuclei Instance Segmentation and Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02671)**  `arXiv:2611.02671`  
  _Rukang Ma, Bingxue Wang, Liwen Zou, Yingying Cao, Zhenghua Cai, Yu Li, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Joint nuclei instance segmentation and classification requires precise boundaries and neighborhood information that helps distinguish morphologically similar cell types. We present TME-ContextNet, a multi-task framework that learns class-conditioned spatial context from existing nuclear annotations and organizes decoding into geometry-related and semantic task groups. Class-conditioned spatial supervision extends nuclear labels into a dense target using Euclidean distance transforms, requiring no additional tissue-region annotation. We derive its nearest-region interpretation and characterize its stability to small annotation perturbations. A local--global context module combines dilated convolution and self-attention, while a grouped task decoder reduces redundant computation. The spatial head supplies training supervision and is omitted during inference. Experiments on PanMix, CoNSeP, and PanNuke yield Dice scores of 80.23%, 65.32%, and 79.13%, and mean multi-class panoptic quality (mPQ+) scores of 58.67%, 35.50%, and 43.74%, respectively. PanNuke results are averaged across three test folds. Target and decoder controls support the combination of distance-based supervision and grouped decoding while identifying their dependence on task configuration. The framework uses 36.40 million parameters, compared with 54.74 million for HoVer-Net. These findings support a compact, context-aware formulation for joint nuclei analysis in computational pathology.
  </details>

- **[Unified Loss-Aware Density Control for 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02044)**  `arXiv:2611.02044`  
  _Tae-Young Kim, Jiwoo Chung, Jae-Pil Heo_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  The efficiency and fidelity of 3D Gaussian Splatting critically depend on adaptive density control, which grows and suppresses Gaussian primitives throughout optimization. However, the standard pipeline still relies on heuristic view-space gradients, scale thresholds, and global opacity resets, rather than explicitly assessing the loss-reducing effect of each split, clone, or opacity update. This mismatch can allocate primitives to already-sufficient regions, miss under-reconstructed structures, and destabilize training through blanket opacity changes. In this work, we recast adaptive density control as a collection of local loss-reduction decisions. We derive efficient Taylor-based per-Gaussian surrogates that predict the objective change caused by three primitive-level operations: splitting, cloning, and opacity decay. This yields a unified loss-aware framework with three components. First, we extend second-order splitting to a normalized joint position-scale space, enabling children to adapt not only their locations but also their anisotropic extents. Second, we formulate duplicate cloning as a surrogate minimization problem, selecting only Gaussians whose duplicated contribution is predicted to improve reconstruction and assigning each child a principled opacity. Third, we replace global opacity reset with selective soft opacity decay that weakens harmful primitives while preserving useful ones. Across standard 3DGS benchmarks, our method produces more targeted primitive allocation and achieves improved rendering quality with comparable or smaller Gaussian budgets compared to baselines.
  </details>

- **[Answer Correction with Verifiable Rewards: A Gemma-Family Study of Multi-View Driving QA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00828)**  `arXiv:2611.00828`  
  _T N Rickesh, Pranav Vinodh, Sowmya Kamath S_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multi-camera driving question answering provides a discrete test of vision-language models, but post-training gains can reflect changed selected answers or improved answer extraction. We investigate this distinction within the Gemma model family using archived, task-linked WaymoQA evaluations. A zero-shot diagnostic on 5,519 test questions spans effective-small, mixture-of-experts, unified, and dense checkpoints, with serving differences disclosed rather than interpreted as architecture effects. The strongest controlled evidence is a matched-harness Gemma-4-12B base/GRPO pair: accuracy rises from 73.78% to 75.43%, a gain of 1.65 percentage points with a scene-cluster bootstrap interval of [+0.84, +2.41]. There are 215 improvements and 124 regressions; 213 improvements start from an extractable but incorrect base answer, and only two recover previously unextractable responses. Crossing correctness with extraction state shows why correct noncompliant outputs cannot be counted as prediction errors. Category counts reveal a critical safety asymmetry: routine perception gains (+5.93 pp) mask a regression in safety-critical hazard prediction (-1.82 pp), demonstrating that unweighted outcome rewards can trade off rare edge cases for aggregate accuracy. Reward saturation describes sampled training dynamics rather than an architectural ceiling. A separate archived Gemma-31B thinking comparison yields no detected average improvement, with uncertainty that does not establish equivalence. These results support a modest answer-selection gain for the recorded tuning configuration and a reproducible diagnostic accounting, without attributing corrected labels to specific grounding mechanisms or claiming superiority over matched supervised tuning.
  </details>

- **[DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00769)**  `arXiv:2611.00769`  
  _Xinyue Huo, Pengfei Chen, Jiannan Ge, Kaiwen Duan, Jiacheng Shao, Yunning Cao, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available atthis https URL
  </details>

- **[VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40131)**  `arXiv:2610.40131`  
  _Zhengdong Hu, Chao Wang, Kaituo Feng, Huanjin Yao, Mingfei Lu, Hehe Fan, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can now process hour-long videos, making extended multi-turn dialogue over a single video a natural mode of use. Sustaining such a dialogue requires more than answering each question in isolation: the model must retrieve and reuse information established earlier in the conversation, both what it has seen and what it has said, an ability we term in-context video memory. Existing video QA benchmarks leave this ability unmeasured: their questions are mutually independent, never reference one another, and each is answerable from the video alone, so nothing ever requires carrying information across turns. We introduce VideoMemBench, in which each sample pairs a single video with a long multi-turn dialogue, whose turns are connected by typed cross-turn dependencies: an Episodic Dependency refers back to a visual episode described in an earlier turn, probing memory of what the model has seen, while an Answer Dependency builds on the model's own earlier answer, probing memory of what the model has said. Every dependency is verified considering two properties: 1) necessity, meaning the question cannot be answered without its earlier turns, and 2) non-leakage, meaning the question does not restate the information from its earlier turns. To enforce these properties, we design a construction pipeline with three LLM roles: a planner, a generator, and a judger, with each dialogue reviewed by human experts. VideoMemBench comprises 326 videos with 2,476 turns, of which 1,387 depend on earlier turns, including multi-parent dependencies and long-range call-back. Among over 20 evaluated open- and closed-source MLLMs, Claude Opus 5 performs the best with an overall score of only 45.7%, highlighting the challenge of in-context video memory. Our dataset and evaluation are released.
  </details>

- **[M-PFT: Angular Margin for Calibrated Prompt-Tuning of Fine-Tuned Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39861)**  `arXiv:2610.39861`  
  _Shihab Aaqil Ahamed, Mohamed Ansaff, Nang Khin Myat Lay Phyu, Udaya Sampath K. Perera Miriya Thanthrige, Chamira U. S. Edussooriya, Ranga Rodrigo, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Prompt-tuning has emerged as a parameter-efficient technique for adapting large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) to downstream tasks while keeping the pre-trained weights frozen. However, prompt-tuned VLMs often suffer from a base-to-novel dual miscalibration problem, where models typically show underconfidence on base classes and overconfidence on novel classes. Current VLM calibration approaches address this dual miscalibration either separately or jointly, but lack a geometric understanding of the hyperspherical embedding space and thus fail to exploit angular discriminative properties to adjust distorted decision boundaries. To address this, we propose M-PFT, a novel angular-margin approach for prompt tuning that introduces two complementary objectives to promote class discriminability and semantic anchoring. This enlarges the angular margin by 1) minimizing the maximum cosine similarity between tunable class embeddings to reduce embedding collapse and 2) minimizing the angular distance between each tunable embedding and its corresponding zero-shot embedding to preserve semantic geometry. Extensive experiments across 9 prompt-tuning methods with various backbones on 15 diverse datasets show that our approach reduces the average calibration error on novel classes, while remaining competitive on base classes and maintaining comparable accuracy. Further analyses reveal that M-PFT effectively adjusts distorted decision boundaries induced by prompt tuning while preserving the pre-trained embedding space, improving calibration with negligible computational overhead.
  </details>

- **[NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39715)**  `arXiv:2610.39715`  
  _Shaokai Zheng_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Accurate oriented detection requires boxes to follow object boundaries, yet small errors in the coupled center, size, and angle estimates can displace long boundaries even when an object is correctly classified. We propose NIF, a plug-in refinement branch that represents box geometry with normal-intersection fields. Given a coarse oriented box, it samples local features at 20 boundary anchors and predicts signed distances along their outward normals. These observations have an exact affine representation in five rectangle parameters; a differentiable projection uses error-aware reliability weights to recover a geometrically consistent box. Tangential pooling preserves the normal-position profile, while the shared projection adds 0.132M parameters. On DOTA-v1.0, NIF obtains 77.98%, 79.03%, and 79.32% mAP with Oriented R-CNN, Strip R-CNN, and LSKNet-S, respectively; LSKNet-S gives the strongest single-scale result among the compared methods. NIF also reaches 68.19% mAP on DIOR-R and improves matched FAIR1M-v1.0 and DIOR-R baselines by 0.30% and 0.71%, respectively. On HRSC2016, it raises mean IoU from 0.867 to 0.888 while reducing field error by 24.5%. Finally, with four different detector frameworks frozen, NIF improves relative AP75 by 1.55-4.16% and COCO-style mAP by 0.37-3.76%, without detector retraining. Upon acceptance of this paper, we will publicly release the code atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Segmentation Confidence for Arbitrary CNNs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37431)**  `arXiv:2610.37431`  
  _Baris Oguz, Xing Yao, Claudia Tawil, Alison Pouch, Brett Byram, Gabriel Arenas, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are widely used for medical image segmentation. However, they lack an inherent measure of confidence. Existing methods for estimating prediction uncertainty often require a custom network architecture and/or dedicated training setups and need to be trained from scratch. In addition, the deduction of a single confidence score per input from the uncertainty maps is not always straightforward. In this study, we explore voxel-based uncertainty estimation methods that can be added to existing segmentation pipelines without training from scratch. We also propose a novel method to estimate a single confidence score from the uncertainty maps. Our evaluations on different ROIs and modalities suggest that our confidence score can predict segmentation performance in unseen data.
  </details>

- **[Full Collapse Is Suboptimal: Controlled Partial Neural Collapse for Long-Tailed Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36460)**  `arXiv:2610.36460`  
  _Hyeontaek Hwang, Cheonghwan Hur, Daeyoung Kim_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Recent long-tailed recognition (LTR) methods incorporate neural collapse (NC) and align features to a fixed Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF) as a uniform target for all classes. However, forcing tail classes to fully collapse over-contracts their samples and weakens generalization. To address this, we propose a controlled partial neural collapse, realized through two coordinated controls on a backbone: the Class-Adaptive Sparse Activation (CASA) classifier and the ETF-constrained adaptive margin (ETF-AM) loss. Rather than forcing a uniform full collapse, this regime allows head classes to collapse along the ETF while tail classes retain within-class diversity. This prevents the tail from being forced into full collapse, which is suboptimal under imbalance. To set the dimensionality of collapse, CASA induces class-related node specialization through feature-conditioned gating so that tail classes occupy their own feature directions. For the clearance axis, ETF-AM applies a frequency-adaptive margin, with smaller margins for head classes and larger for tail classes. On CIFAR100-LT, ImageNet-LT, Places-LT, and iNaturalist-2018, our method achieves the best overall accuracy over prior methods. In the empirical analysis, within-class spread increases monotonically from head to tail classes, consistent with tail classes retaining variability rather than fully collapsing.
  </details>

- **[Fovea-JEPA: Overcoming Geometric Blind Spots in V-JEPA for Camera Motion Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34033)**  `arXiv:2610.34033`  
  _Xiangkun Shi, Hanhui Li, Shiyue Zhang, Xiaodan Liang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Camera motion recognition requires separating viewpoint changes caused by camera translation, rotation, or zoom from object motion and scene dynamics. Video-language models often rely on semantic cues and struggle with the geometric evidence needed for this task. Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures such as V-JEPA offer strong spatio-temporal representations, but our experiments suggest that they underrepresent geometric cues in some regions. Under temporal-reversal supervision, V-JEPA improves overall but degrades on several motion families, whereas a weaker geometry-oriented VGGT predictor improves across all families. We refer to these geometrically underrepresented regions as geometric blind spots and propose Fovea-JEPA to identify and address them. Using V-JEPA as the base model and VGGT as a geometry expert, we construct intervention pseudo-labels from their prediction errors to weakly supervise a blind-spot predictor. The predictor produces token-wise response maps, which are aggregated into a clip-level intervention score to guide adaptive fusion of visual and geometric features. This selective intervention introduces complementary geometric information while preserving reliable visual predictions. Experiments on CameraMotionDataset, CameraBench, and ShotBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Fovea-JEPA, with gains of 9.67, 8.67, and 24.38 percentage points over previously reported state-of-the-art baselines, respectively. Code and models will be released upon acceptance.
  </details>

- **[Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31111)**  `arXiv:2610.31111`  
  _Yuanze Hu, Zhichao Yang, Junwei Jing, Xin Yang, Wenxuan Liu, Tinghai Zhang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Detailed image captioning is usually framed as an amount problem: a model should mention more visual facts while avoiding hallucination. However, autoregressive VLMs generate captions as ordered sequences, and later generations may be produced under weaker or noisier visual grounding. We therefore argue that long-form captioning should be studied not only by what facts are mentioned, but also by where they appear. We introduce a position-aware rubric representation that decomposes dense human references into atomic visual claims, verifies generated captions against those claims, and induces a quartile-wise composition of supported, hallucinated, and generic content. This lens reveals two qualitatively different failures in long captions: models tend to produce unsupported specificity in the middle, while the final portion often escapes into vague, non-evidential language rather than simply accumulating more hallucination. A same-reference human control does not exhibit these patterns; additional human audits examine the visual validity of the induced labels. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose PAGER (Position-Aware Grounded Evidence Reinforcement), a GRPO training objective with separate signals for supported fine-grained middle evidence, evidence-bearing tail continuation, claim coverage, and content-aware length control. The result is a closed loop: the same ordered claim representation identifies where long captions fail and supplies the position-specific reward needed to repair those failures. Experiments on detailed-caption benchmarks show that PAGER improves position-wise grounding and pairwise caption preference while preserving competitive global caption quality.
  </details>

- **[No Frames, Just Frequencies: Bandwidth-Efficient Deployment-Time Adaptation for Smart Glasses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29607)**  `arXiv:2610.29607`  
  _Francesco Corti, Moritz Becker, Olga Saukh_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Deep neural networks deployed on smart glasses must adapt to changes in the distribution of incoming data while adhering to strict privacy and device constraints. We present No Frames, Just Frequencies, a bandwidth-efficient source-assisted adaptation framework that characterizes distribution shifts using compact frequency descriptors computed on-device. Rather than transmitting camera frames, the glasses compute and send frequency descriptors to a host device that contains a replica of the model. The host device maps the received frequency descriptor to a distribution shift operator that synthesizes out-of-distribution data and adapts a model replica using a pre-defined adaptation protocol. We evaluate the framework on mixtures of ImageNet-C corruptions using convolution-based (ConvNeXtV2-Femto), self-attention-based (DeiT-Tiny), and hybrid (TinyViT-5M) vision models, on person classification (Visual Wake Words), and on object detection (MS-COCO). Our results reveal that adaptation driven solely by the transmitted descriptors recovers $93-95\%$ of the supervised oracle adaptation gain on all three architectures, $82\%$ on Visual Wake Words and $94$--$98\%$ on MS-COCO. Notably, adaptation quality degrades gracefully as the descriptor resolution decreases from $224 $ to $28$ pixels, consistently across architectures, enabling bandwidth reductions from $213\times$ to $784\times$ across the frequency descriptors.
  </details>

- **[Gaze2HOI: Gaze-Aware Intention Disambiguation for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27877)**  `arXiv:2610.27877`  
  _Chuanyang Ma, Chenye Wang, Yixuan Wang, Huiling Zhou, Man Zhang, Xingqun Qi, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Anticipating how users will interact with their surroundings is essential for proactive systems that provide timely assistance in extended reality and embodied applications. Prior work typically forecasts hand-object interactions directly from historical observations, leaving intention and contact geometry implicit. However, similar observation histories can precede semantically or geometrically distinct futures. Inspired by behavioral evidence that gaze can provide early cues for underlying intention, we propose Gaze2HOI, a gaze-aware framework that formulates hand-object interaction forecasting as a hierarchical problem comprising intention inference, contact grounding, and coupled hand-object motion generation. Specifically, Gaze2HOI first weights gaze cues by fixation strength and recency, and uses them to modulate the visual representations of a vision-language model (VLM) through Temporal Gaze Saliency Modulation (TGSM), thereby reducing semantic ambiguity in intention inference. Subsequently, an Anticipatory Contact Grounding (ACG) module maps these structured intentions into explicit contact, support, and placement fields, effectively mitigating geometric ambiguity. Driven by these explicit conditions, a diffusion-based model jointly generates the six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) object trajectories and future articulated motion of both hands. To evaluate Gaze2HOI, we further introduce EgoAIM, a phase-aware benchmark that organizes egocentric hand-object interactions into four phases defined by evolving hand-object relations and provides fine-grained intention annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Gaze2HOI achieves state-of-the-art performance in both intention inference and motion forecasting, even approaching oracle-level end-to-end performance in specific interaction phases. Project page:this https URL.
  </details>

- **[SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23979)**  `arXiv:2610.23979`  
  _Cassandra Parent, Isha Agarwal, Kumail Alhamoud, Charikleia Moraitaki, Rafiya Javed, Walter Gerych, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are the backbone of many state-of-the-art multimodal systems, but often encode spurious and harmful associations from their training data. While prior work focuses on removing known biases from VLMs, methods for discovering unanticipated associations for retrieval tasks remain underexplored. We introduce SPELUNKA, an automated, inference-time framework for finding unanticipated distributional biases for retrieval tasks in VLMs without pre-specified labeled subgroups, inference-time human supervision, or model fine-tuning. Given a concept of interest, SPELUNKA generates captions for related images, extracts relevant entities from captions, and selects semantically meaningful associations. A frequency-based detection rule then identifies spurious associations by measuring over- or under-representation of these attributes in a VLM's top-ranked outputs relative to their full dataset distribution. We evaluate SPELUNKA across four datasets, and find that it 1) successfully recovers both synthetic and naturally occurring spurious correlations, 2) achieves an average AUROC of 0.93 across four datasets in identifying images strongly associated with a query, and 3) outperforms baselines in finding features that are strongly associated with a given query.
  </details>

- **[FuseAdapt: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Semantic Segmentation with Missing Modalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21779)**  `arXiv:2610.21779`  
  _Xin Zhang, Robby T. Tan_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multi-modal semantic segmentation benefits from complementary sensors, but this benefit is fragile when some modalities are degraded or missing at test time. Many existing methods rely on dedicated fusion modules or multi-branch cross-modal encoders, and the fusion often becomes unreliable when modalities are absent, leading to substantial performance drops. We propose FuseAdapt, a parameter-efficient framework that performs fusion within the adaptation space of a frozen vision foundation model (VFM), exploring whether VFM priors can serve as an effective shared backbone for multi-modal segmentation. Instead of attaching a standalone fusion network, FuseAdapt assigns each modality a lightweight adaptation branch and performs adaptation-space fusion by keeping Q/V low-rank adaptation private to each modality and routing only FFN low-rank residual activations across modalities inside the frozen backbone. The pretrained VFM remains fixed while modality-specific corrections and explicit cross-modal interaction are learned through the adaptation paths. To handle missing modalities, we further introduce Predictive Modality Modeling (PMM), a direct representation-level objective for cross-modal redundancy. During training, PMM masks a target modality and predicts its embedding from the visible ones, supervised by a teacher target computed under full-modality input. PMM is used only during training and adds no inference-time overhead. Across three multi-modal segmentation benchmarks (MCubeS, DELIVER, MUSES), FuseAdapt consistently improves both modality-complete and modality-incomplete segmentation with a small trainable budget, yielding up to +3.01 mIoU under full modalities and +11.25 mIoU under missing modalities over prior state-of-the-art. Project page:this https URL
  </details>

- **[CoDeFont: One-Shot Font Generation via Multi-Scale Factor-Specific Representation Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21364)**  `arXiv:2610.21364`  
  _Rejoy Chakraborty, Prasun Roy, Saumik Bhattacharya, Umapada Pal_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  One-shot Font Generation (OFG) aims to synthesize a target glyph by transferring the stylistic characteristics of a single reference glyph while preserving the structure of the target character. However, accurately capturing font style from a single reference image remains challenging due to the limited stylistic information available in a single glyph, and this challenge is further amplified for complex scripts. We propose CoDeFont, a script-agnostic OFG framework that addresses this challenge through multi-level style-content factorization and progressive style-content reconciliation. CoDeFont independently aggregates complementary style and structural information across multiple spatial levels to obtain factor-specific representations, while a contrastive objective explicitly encourages separation between style and content embeddings. During reconstruction, the disentangled representations are progressively injected through multi-level style conditioning, enabling stylistic information to be incorporated at different decoding resolutions while preserving the underlying glyph structure. We evaluate CoDeFont on structurally distinct Bengali and Latin scripts across seen and unseen font styles. Extensive quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate consistent improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed framework for OFG across diverse writing systems.
  </details>

- **[ELMA: Benchmarking Anaphoric Compositions for Long-Term Text-to-Motion Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13549)**  `arXiv:2610.13549`  
  _Shun Kato, Dixin Yang, Kotaro Amaya, Yuiga Wada, Kazumi Fukuda, Takashi Shibuya, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Text-guided long-term human motion generation is essential for applications such as continuously operating digital avatars. Despite recent progress on short clips, existing models struggle with multi-segment instructions that involve anaphora, where constraints established in earlier segments must be preserved over time. In this paper, we introduce a novel task of long-term motion generation from such anaphoric compositions. To address this gap, we present ELMA, an episodic long-term motion dataset with dense segment-level annotations that preserve cross-segment dependencies. Built via a fully automated collection and filtering pipeline, ELMA extracts high-quality, continuous 30-second clips from in-the-wild videos, capturing the episodic narratives necessary for long-range state modeling. Using ELMA, we benchmark representative long-term motion generation models under independent and anaphoric instruction settings, and study whether contextual fine-tuning improves long-range state modeling. Our extensive experiments provide insights into the capabilities and limitations of existing models in handling context-dependent instructions. These findings highlight the challenge of modeling cross-segment dependencies and offer valuable directions for developing more coherent and semantically consistent long-term motion generation models.
  </details>

- **[WoodBR-Cross: A public wood-image dataset and individual-tree-disjoint benchmark for species identification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12676)**  `arXiv:2610.12676`  
  _Daniel Casanova, Alexandre Bahia Gontijo, Arnaldo Candido Junior, Silvana Nisgoski, Pedro Luiz de Paula Filho_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Wood identification supports timber inspection and species conservation. However, benchmarks can overestimate generalization when photographs of the same tree occur in training and test sets. We present WoodBR-Cross: 4,875 transverse-surface microscope images, 38 operational taxonomic classes and 303 catalogue-linked trees. A species subset contains 3,406 images, 20 classes and 214 trees. Task A evaluates all classes using duplicate-aware image partitions. B1 partitions images of the species subset, allowing different photographs of one tree across partitions. B2 keeps each tree's photographs together, testing recognition of unseen trees on the same subset. We benchmark three backbones and baselines across three folds and five training seeds. Validation-selected ConvNeXt-Tiny achieves B2 tree-level macro-F1 of 0.8621 +/- 0.0317; frozen DINOv2 features yield 0.9000 +/- 0.0722. Values are means +/- SD across three folds; fine-tuned scores are seed-averaged within folds. This resource supports reproducible, group-aware evaluation.
  </details>

- **[Disentangling Dual Image References in Frequency Aware Diffusion Models for Personalized Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07684)**  `arXiv:2610.07684`  
  _Haipeng Liu, Yang Wang, Meng Wang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Personalized image generation aims to synthesize text-driven images conditioned on reference images, while mainly casting the generation as image customization for foreground and style transfer for background. Previous arts of diffusion models suffers from the text misalignment with background for image customization and foreground for style transfer during the denoising process. Such facts, as we observed, rooted from the entanglement among hybrid frequency bands during the denoising process. In particular, the low-frequency band primarily captures color information, mid-frequency band encodes global structure, while high-frequency band corresponds to local texture. Besides, the early (high-noise) denoising stage mainly focuses on the low-and-mid frequency bands, while the late (low-noise) denoising stage progressively exhibits the high-frequency band, which, all together, overwhelm the text prompt guidance, suffering from the heavy reliance on reference image. To address such salient limitation, in this paper, we study personalized generation based on dual references - customization and color style reference - to propose a paradigm to disentangle these Dual image references within Frequency-aware Diffusion Models, dubbed Dual-FDM, to simultaneously tackle two crucial personalized image generation tasks: customization style transfer and color style transfer, by disentangling different frequency bands via mask strategy within frequency domain. We further compute the ratio of information entropy of the substituted frequency bands to adaptively modulate the denoising timesteps between the early and late stages. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of Dual-FDM over the state-of-the-art diffusion models for personalized image generation. Our code can be accessed fromthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Salvation Lies Within: Eliciting Inherent Style Transfer in Step-Distilled Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05066)**  `arXiv:2610.05066`  
  _Shengyin Sun, Yiming Li, Yingzhao Lian, Xing Li, Xingzhi Zhou, Anxin Tian, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Adapting step-distilled text-to-image (T2I) models through post-training incurs additional computational costs and affects native few-step generation behavior. This motivates a complementary route beyond style-specific adaptation: drawing on the visual knowledge already encoded in step-distilled T2I models to elicit stylistic capabilities through language. Pursuing this direction requires textual guidance that captures how visual attributes jointly define a style and remain applicable as the depicted content changes. To explore this approach, we introduce StyleForge, a fully automatic, training-free framework that expresses reference styles as reusable rendering instructions. By integrating overall rendering characteristics with local color and lighting behavior, StyleForge organizes visual evidence from reference images into a coherent specification of how the target style should be expressed. The specification is then compiled into textual guidance that can be reused across content prompts, enabling frozen step-distilled T2I models to render different subjects and scenes in the reference style while retaining native few-step generation. Extensive experiments show relative gains of up to 29.47\% in generation quality scores over the strongest baseline, while Pareto analysis indicates that improved stylization is accompanied by strong adherence to the requested content. Code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Beyond Spatial-Domain Supervision: A Relation Constrained Space for Multi-Modal Image Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38968)**  `arXiv:2609.38968`  
  _Zeyu Wang, Mingyu Ge, Haiyu Song, Haoran Duan_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multi-modal image fusion (MMIF) aims to form a single image by integrating shared information, preserving complementary cues, and coordinating cross-modal conflicts across modalities. However, due to the absence of ground-truth fused images, existing MMIF supervision commonly uses spatial-domain sources or gradient variants as surrogate ground truths, making the supervision mechanism inherently misaligned with the goal of MMIF and causing pixel-level compromise or modality bias. To address this, we propose a relation-constrained supervision paradigm that moves fusion supervision from the spatial domain to a learned relation space. Instead of forcing the fused image to approximate the sources, we use frozen pretrained representation models as information providers and design a learnable feature adapter to align heterogeneous DINO and CLIP features into a unified supervision space. The adapter infers three relation parameters, namely sharedness, dominance, and coordination radius, which define three losses corresponding to the MMIF's goal. To make this space reliable, we devise a self-supervised contrastive ranking objective tailored to the adapter and couple it with the fusion network through alternating optimization. Extensive experiments show that the proposed supervision space yields significant gains regardless of which mainstream backbone the fusion network adopts, offering a supervision paradigm better aligned with the goal of MMIF. Code:this http URL.
  </details>

- **[Drag as Evidence: Motion-Grounded Latent Recomposition for Drag-Based Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36755)**  `arXiv:2609.36755`  
  _Xinyu Pu, Hongsong Wang, Jie Gui, Pan Zhou_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Modern image editors excel at semantic manipulation and visual synthesis, yet remain limited in precise spatial control, motivating the development of drag-based editing. However, existing drag-based methods often struggle to balance drag accuracy with natural, plausible, and intent-aligned generation. We propose MoRe-Drag, a motion-grounded drag-based editing method. Our key insight is to treat pixel-space warping as coarse motion evidence, and to inject this evidence into the generative sampling trajectory. Specifically, MoRe-Drag performs region-aware latent recomposition over refinement, inpainting, and preservation regions, coupled with stage-adaptive conditioning that progressively shifts from motion-grounded structure formation to semantic refinement. We further support a no-manual-instruction interface by adapting the MLLM-based text encoder for drag-aware instruction inference. Experiments on DragBench-SR and DragBench-DR show that MoRe-Drag substantially improves drag precision over strong base editors and achieves superior drag accuracy among SOTA drag-based methods, while delivering strong semantic consistency and visually realistic results. Project page:this https URL.
  </details>

- **[SceneScaffold: Active Scene-State Construction for Unified 3D Scene Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33518)**  `arXiv:2609.33518`  
  _Xiangqi Li, Libo Huang, Jiarui Zhao, Weilun Feng, Chuanguang Yang, Zhulin An, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Recent 3D large multimodal models (3D-LMMs) rely on a visual bottleneck to compress complex 3D scene evidence into a limited number of visual tokens compatible with large language models (LLMs). Current visual bottlenecks, however, often passively compress heterogeneous 3D evidence into a homogeneous object-centric token sequence, leaving the spatial organization of the scene under-represented. This under-representation forces the LLM to recover spatial relations from a flattened token sequence, leading to unstable reasoning in relation-intensive and spatially ambiguous scenes. To address this issue, we propose SceneScaffold, an active scene-state construction framework for unified 3D scene understanding. SceneScaffold reformulates the visual bottleneck from a passive feature compressor into an active scene organizer, constructing a role-aware spatial scaffold before language reasoning. Specifically, SceneScaffold organizes superpoint-level visual evidence into scene-state components with distinct structural roles: entity states preserve core object semantics, scene-frame states maintain spatial references via boundary and region anchors, relation states encode object-environment interaction cues, and a global summary provides compact context. Through this role-aware construction, SceneScaffold provides the LLM with a spatially organized scene representation before language reasoning. Experiments on unified 3D scene understanding tasks, including 3D visual grounding, question answering, and dense captioning, demonstrate the effectiveness of SceneScaffold, while diagnostic results further show its applicability to relation-intensive and spatially ambiguous cases. Code is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[Identity-Consistent Analysis of Long-Shot Windsurfing Video: A Domain-Specific Offline Tracking System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24492)**  `arXiv:2609.24492`  
  _Bertil Braun, Felix Muehlenberend_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Long-shot windsurfing video combines small targets, large camera pans, prolonged overlaps, and rapidly changing backgrounds. The desired output is not a generic MOT trace but a separate, stable rider-relative video for each surfer; one false identity merge can invalidate an otherwise useful result. We present an offline analysis system that detects surfers, forms conservative local tracklets, links them globally with camera-compensated motion and a foreground-masked sail-color descriptor, and uses two pose keypoints on the rig to drive a rider-relative virtual camera. The tracking stage is evaluated on 21 manually reconstructed development videos containing 41,004 retained observations. On this fixed-observation protocol, the production system achieves 0.957 pairwise precision, 0.918 recall, and 0.937 F1, compared with 0.792 F1 for OC-SORT and 0.828 for BoT-SORT. Compared with OC-SORT, it reduces fragmentation excess from 845 to 42, but nine of its 95 output tracks mix rider identities and these errors affect seven of the 21 videos.
  </details>

- **[CleanVideo: Adaptive Concept Erasure for Text-to-Video Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20267)**  `arXiv:2609.20267`  
  _Junchi Liao, Hongji Li, Wenrui Zhou, Lijie Hu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Concept erasure aims to selectively eliminate undesired visual semantics from pre-trained generative models without compromising their general utility. Extending concept erasure from images to video is nontrivial. Target concepts emerge gradually and vary across frames and denoising steps. As a result, fixed interventions may miss the target or introduce blurring, jitter, and content distortion. We propose CleanVideo, a selective erasure framework that performs low-dimensional subspace intervention controlled by a tri-modal gating mechanism. By jointly processing spatiotemporal visual features, timestep signals, and textual semantics, CleanVideo determines where, when, and whether to intervene, steering erased content toward natural surrogate concepts when such surrogates can be clearly defined while preserving non-target content. Experiments on three video diffusion models show that CleanVideo effectively erases target concepts while maintaining visual fidelity and temporal coherence, outperforming existing baselines under frame-level and video-level evaluations and under concept-recovery attacks when the protected pipeline remains intact.
  </details>

- **[Zero-Shot Cross-Material Ptychographic Phase Reconstruction Using Deep Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13969)**  `arXiv:2609.13969`  
  _Wen-Chun Lin, Kuan-Peng Chen, Nan-Yow Chen, Yu-Chee Tseng, Jen-Jee Chen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Ptychographic phase reconstruction is commonly formulated as an iterative inverse problem, requiring repeated object-probe updates and resulting in substantial computational cost for large-scale 4D-STEM data. We present a direct local-to-global learning framework that reconstructs full-field phase maps from diffraction measurements without iterative refinement during inference. The proposed network predicts local wrapped-phase patches from individual diffraction patterns using a sine-cosine representation, and the predictions are assembled into a full-field reconstruction using calibrated scan positions and Gaussian-weighted stitching. To evaluate generalization beyond the training domain, the model is trained on one material and directly applied to another in a zero-shot setting without target-domain fine-tuning. Experiments on AuPd and MoS$_2$ demonstrate consistent cross-material transfer in both directions, with the proposed method achieving the best full-field MSE, PSNR, and MS-SSIM among the evaluated learning-based methods. Compared with the iterative ePIE approach, the proposed direct local-to-global pipeline reduces end-to-end reconstruction time by approximately 10$\times$, demonstrating its potential for efficient and transferable ptychographic reconstruction.
  </details>

- **[MEOX: Modality-Conditioned Routing Before Fusion in a Compact Earth Observation Encoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05351)**  `arXiv:2609.05351`  
  _Mohanad Albughdadi_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multimodal Earth Observation models often fuse radar and optical inputs early, limiting sensor-conditioned processing, or maintain separate sensor streams through the encoder, increasing computational cost. We present MEOX (Multimodal Earth Observation with eXperts), which delays fusion until after a shared mixture-of-experts block that processes Sentinel-2 and ascending and descending Sentinel-1 streams independently. Co-located patches are then fused with validity-aware weights into a single sequence processed by fourteen shared blocks, reducing the sequence length from 3N + 5 to N + 5 tokens for N patches. We pretrain the 2.939M-parameter encoder on 1.228M MMEarth64 samples using masked radar-optical reconstruction. Under the reported frozen-transfer protocols, MEOX reaches 90.56% average class accuracy on EuroSAT and 64.42% mean intersection over union (mIoU) on cashew segmentation, 2.26 and 5.02 points above the strongest reported cross-sensor mixture-of-experts (CSMoE) variants. Full-encoder adaptation increases BigEarthNet micro-average precision from 57.22% to 72.95%. In a controlled same-corpus test using synthetic random patch removal, masking 75% of Sentinel-2 patches reduces WorldCover mIoU from 30.45% to 26.53% when both Sentinel-1 streams remain available; with Sentinel-2 alone, mIoU falls to 13.81%. For identical zeroed optical patches, declaring them missing through the validity mechanism improves mIoU from 19.42% to 26.53%. These results characterize a compact route-then-fuse encoder that retains sensor-conditioned processing and uses complementary radar observations when optical inputs are incomplete.
  </details>

- **[Improved Automatic Target Recognition in Synthetic Aperture Sonar Imagery Using Large Deep Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01800)**  `arXiv:2609.01800`  
  _C.J. Moore, Alex Hurt, Jordan Malof_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) in Synthetic Aperture Sonar (SAS) is often underpinned by deep neural networks (DNNs). Recent research has focused on relatively low-capacity DNNs (i.e., relatively fewer trainable parameters) to avoid overfitting on the small training datasets that are typically available for SAS. However, recent research has found that increasing DNN capacity often improves performance, even when training data is scarce. Motivated by this emerging finding - termed the double descent phenomenon - this work investigates the use of especially high-capacity DNNs for SAS-ATR. We evaluate the performance of several state-of-the-art DNN architectures as we increase their model capacity. We examine performance in a realistic leave-one-geo-location-out cross-validation scheme. We find that increasing model capacity often increases performance substantially, and is never harmful. All of our large models significantly outperform two baseline models from recent publications.
